questions.question: At which of the following places does river Ganga bifurcate to form its distributary called Bhagirathi-Hooghly?

questions.question: What is the site of transmission of electric nerve impulses between two nerve cells (neurons) or between a neuron and a gland or muscle cell (effector)?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **"**__**Synapse**__**"**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

__**Synapse**__** :**

__
 
• The site of transmission of electric nerve impulses between two nerve cells (neurons) or between a neuron and a gland or muscle cell (effector). 
 
• In the **central nervous system,** a synapse is a **small gap** at the end of a neuron that allows a signal to pass from one neuron to the next.
 
• Synapses are found where nerve cells **connect** with other nerve cells.
 
• Synapses are **vital to the transmission **of worried impulses from one neuron to some other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**__Dendrite__ :**

__
 
• **Dendrites** are **projections of a neuron** (nerve cell) that receive signals (information) from other neurons.
 
• The transfer of information from one neuron to another is achieved through chemical **signals and electric impulses**, that is, electrochemical signals.
 
• The information transfer is usually received at the dendrites through chemical signals, then it travels to the cell body (soma), continues along the neuronal **axon as electric** **impulses**, and it is finally transferred onto the next neuron at the synapse, which is the place where the two neurons exchange information through chemical signals.

**Axon__ :**

__
 
• **Axon**, also called **nerve fiber,** a portion of a nerve cell (neuron) that carries nerve impulses away from the cell body.
 
• A neuron typically has one axon that connects it with other neurons or with muscle or gland cells.
 
• Some axons may be quite long, reaching, for example, from the **spinal cord down to a toe.**
 
• Most axons of vertebrates are enclosed in a myelin sheath, which increases the speed of impulse transmission; some large axons may transmit impulses at speeds up to **90 meters (300 feet) per second.**

**Myelin sheath__ :**

 
• **Myelin** is an insulating layer or sheath that forms around nerves, including those in the** brain and spinal cord.**
 
• It is made up of protein and fatty substances.
 
• This** myelin sheath **allows electrical impulses to transmit quickly and efficiently along with the nerve cells.
 
• If myelin is damaged, these impulses slow down.
 
• This can cause diseases such as **multiple sclerosis.**

questions.question: ______ is a vestigial hollow tube that is closed at one end and is attached at the other end to the cecum, a pouch-like beginning of the large intestine into which the small intestine empties its contents.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**"Appendix"**__.

**Explanation :**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

__**Appendix**__** :**

__
 
• The **appendix** is a **finger-like, blind-ended tube** linked to the cecum, from which it develops withinside the **embryo**.
 
• In particular, it can function as a reservoir for useful **intestine bacteria.**
 
• The human appendix **averages are 9 cm.**
 
• One theory is that the appendix acts as a storehouse for good bacteria, “**rebooting**” the **digestive system **after diarrheal illnesses.
 
• Some experts believe the appendix is just a useless remnant from our evolutionary past.
 
• Surgical removal of the appendix causes **no observable health problems.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__**Spleen**__** :**

__
 
• The spleen is the largest organ in the** lymphatic system.**
 
• It is an important organ for keeping bodily fluids balanced, but it is possible to live without it.
 
• The spleen is located under the ribcage and above the stomach in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen.
 
• A spleen is soft and generally looks **purple**. 

**Ileum**__** :**

__
 
• **Ileum**, the final and **longest** segment of the **small intestine.**
 
• It is specifically responsible for the absorption of **vitamin B12** and the reabsorption of conjugated bile salts.
 
• The **ileum** is about **3.5 meters** (11.5 feet) long (or about three-fifths the length of the small intestine) and extends from the middle section of the small intestine to the ileocecal valve, which empties into the colon (large intestine). 

**Duodenum__ :**

 
• The **duodenum** is the first of the three parts of the small intestine that receives partially digested food from the stomach and begins with the absorption of nutrients.
 
• It is directly attached to the** pylorus of the stomach.**
 
• It has a** C-shape, **which is closely related to the head of the pancreas and consists of four sections: **superior**, **descending**, **horizontal**, and **ascending** parts.
